output.question: What are the key takeaways from Anthropic's S-1 filing?
output.answer: As of November 11, 2026, Anthropic's October 26 S-1 shows extraordinary growth but a still loss-making, capital-intensive model: revenue reached $16.286 billion in the six months ended June 30, 2026, while net loss was $80.748 billion, including a $72.388 billion fair-value loss on convertible notes, derivative liabilities and SAFEs. The filing highlights unusually strong enterprise traction—more than 11,900 customers generating at least $100,000 on a trailing-twelve-month basis and approximately 900% net revenue retention as of September 30, 2026—but says this demand must be converted into cash to fund large, mostly fixed compute and infrastructure obligations. Governance is deliberately mission-oriented and concentrated: the Long-Term Benefit Trust generally elects a majority of the board, while a single Class F share held by the founders' LLC carries 50.1% of general voting power; the filing also emphasizes that AI misuse, safeguard failures, regulation and execution around power/compute are material risks. The proposed IPO is not yet priced: Anthropic says it intends to list as ANT, but the share count and price range had not been determined and the registration statement was not yet effective.

key_facts.fact: For the six months ended June 30, 2026, Anthropic reported $16.286 billion of revenue, $16.979 billion of operating expenses, a $693 million operating loss, and an $80.748 billion net loss; the net loss included a $72.388 billion change in fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities and SAFEs.

As of September 30, 2026, Anthropic reported more than 11,900 customers with at least $100,000 of trailing-twelve-month revenue, more than 1,900 with at least $1 million, approximately 250 with at least $10 million, and approximately 900% net revenue retention.
As of June 30, 2026, Anthropic said it had raised $141.1 billion of capital and held $112.4 billion in cash and cash equivalents plus $19.3 billion in short-term investments.

The Long-Term Benefit Trust generally has authority to elect and remove Class T directors, who will constitute a majority of the authorized board, while one Class F share held by the founders' LLC will carry 50.1% of total voting power on general stockholder matters.

Anthropic says its compute and infrastructure commitments are substantial fixed obligations, including minimum-purchase and take-or-pay terms, while much of its revenue is consumption-based and not subject to long-term customer commitments.

Anthropic warns that safeguards are incomplete and may be circumvented, and that model misuse—including assistance with chemical, biological or other dangerous weapons—could create real-world harm, legal liability, regulatory action and loss of customer trust.

Anthropic intends to list its Class A common stock on Nasdaq under the symbol ANT, but the number of shares and price range had not been determined; its announcement said the registration statement had not yet become effective.

passages.quote: More than 11,900 customers with $100,000 or more of revenue on a TTM basis; More than 1,900 customers with $1 million or more of revenue on a TTM basis; Approximately 250 customers with $10 million or more of revenue on a TTM basis.

Our Class F common stock will be entitled to an aggregate number of votes that equals 50.1% of the total voting power of our outstanding shares of capital stock with respect to matters submitted to stockholders generally.
These commitments represent substantial fixed obligations.
The number of shares of Class A common stock to be offered and the price range for the proposed offering have not yet been determined.

caveats: The S-1 is a preliminary registration statement; offering size, price range and certain aggregate compute-commitment figures are blank or not yet determined in the version reviewed.
The six-month 2026 net loss is heavily affected by non-cash fair-value changes, so it is not a straightforward measure of recurring operating performance.
Customer counts and net revenue retention are company-defined operating metrics, and the filing warns that historical results and interim results may not predict future performance.
